title: 8. Predicting What Comes Next: Sequences and Progressions

q.t: What is the next term of 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, …?
q.e: Triangular numbers: the gaps go 2, 3, 4, 5, so add 6.

q.t: What is the next term of 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, …?
q.e: Square numbers: 6² = 36 (the gaps are the odd numbers 3, 5, 7, 9, 11).

q.t: Using uₙ = 2n − 1, find the 53rd odd number.
q.e: Substitute n = 53 straight into the explicit rule.

q.t: What is the common difference of the AP 11, 7, 3, −1, …?
q.e: Subtract a term from the next one: 7 − 11 = −4. A decreasing AP has negative d.

q.t: What is the common ratio of the GP 3, 6, 12, 24, …?
q.e: Divide a term by the one before: 6 ÷ 3 = 2.
n(n + 1)/2 = 10 × 11 / 2. Pair 1 with 10, 2 with 9, … — 5 pairs of 11.

q.t: Which sequence is an arithmetic progression?
Which sequence is a geometric progression?
q.e: Each term is 3 times the one before: a constant ratio.

q.t: Next term of the Virahānka–Fibonacci sequence 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, …?
q.e: Each term is the sum of the two before it.

q.t: A sequence is t₁ = 1, tₙ = tₙ₋₁ + 3. What is t₄?
q.e: 1, 4, 7, 10 — add 3 each time. This is a recursive rule.

q.t: Find the 10th term of the AP 3, 8, 13, 18, …
q.e: a + (n − 1)d = 3 + 9 × 5. Nine steps take you from the 1st to the 10th term.

q.t: Which term of 2n − 1 (the odd numbers) is 137?
Is 471 a term of sₙ = 5n − 2?
q.e: 5n − 2 = 471 gives n = 94.6; positions must be counting numbers.

Find the 17th triangular number.
q.e: The nth triangular number is n(n + 1)/2 = 17 × 18 / 2.

q.t: A taxi charges ₹200 plus ₹40 per km. What is the fare for 10 km (in ₹)?
q.e: The fares 240, 280, 320, … form an AP; tₙ = 200 + 40n.

q.e: Each stage keeps 3 of 4 equal parts: (3/4)².
